about: flattree's mutants (wf10 DOD DF1): each law's mutant, killed by `ergo test` of its package or by a case, and the edits no law or case sees, which TestFlatTreeAgreesWithControl in cmd/ergo (JSONTestSuite, generated documents and the workload, three sides against a reference on encoding/json) kills. Package tree is examples/jsonparse's package json under a new name: its law-killed mutants are kept here; the ones only TestJSONParseAgreesWithControl kills stay in examples/jsonparse's ledger, which judges the same code.

mutants.name: flattree-tree-pointer-escapes-slash-first
mutants.rule: A pointer escapes ~ before /, so a key with a / is written ~1, not ~01 (law tree.PointersReachTheirPlaces).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-pointer-tilde-one-is-tilde
mutants.rule: In a pointer's token, ~1 stands for / (law tree.PointersReachTheirPlaces).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-quote-keeps-backslash
mutants.rule: The printers escape a backslash, so the text reads back as the value (law tree.PrintParsesBack).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-escape-b-is-form-feed
mutants.rule: The escape \b is the byte 0x08 (law tree.PrintParsesBack: the printer writes 0x08 as \b).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-zero-takes-digits
mutants.rule: No digit follows a leading 0 (law tree.Numeral.ZeroEndsItsInteger).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-exponent-takes-no-sign
mutants.rule: An exponent may have a sign before its digits (law tree.Numeral.ExponentTakesASign).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-zero-takes-no-fraction
mutants.rule: 0.5 is a number (law tree.Numeral.FractionFollowsZero).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-workload-raw-tab
mutants.rule: The workload is JSON: a tab in its strings is escaped (law workload.DocumentIsJSON; the bug the first receipt run found).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-span-keeps-escape
mutants.rule: A string with an escape is decoded, not kept as its span (law flat.FlatEqualsTree).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-intern-forgets
mutants.rule: Interning remembers a text, so one text has one id (law flat.KeysAreInterned).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-array-depth-short
mutants.rule: An array is one deeper than its deepest item (law flat.FlatEqualsTree compares the stats).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-keys-counted-twice
mutants.rule: stats counts distinct keys (law flat.FlatEqualsTree).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-held-not-reset
mutants.rule: A closed object takes its members off the held stack (law flat.FlatEqualsTree).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-stack-not-reset
mutants.rule: A closed array takes its items off the stack (law flat.FlatEqualsTree).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-false-is-true
mutants.rule: The view of false is false (law flat.ViewRoundTrips).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-number-short
mutants.rule: A number's span is all its bytes (law flat.FlatEqualsTree).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-view-number-len-is-offset
mutants.rule: A number's view is its offset and its length (law flat.ViewRoundTrips).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-pointer-first-member-only
mutants.rule: A pointer's token is looked for among all the members, the last first (law flat.PointersReachTheTreesPlaces).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-root-is-first
mutants.rule: The root is the last value put: children come first (law flat.ChildrenStayInside).

mutants.name: flattree-tree-stats-bools-twice
mutants.rule: The plain twin's stats count each bool once (law flat.FlatEqualsTree; case stats-tree).

mutants.name: flattree-app-path-on-one-line
mutants.rule: path prints the value in jq's layout (case path-object).

mutants.name: flattree-flat-depth-limit-one-past
mutants.rule: Nesting fails one past tree.MaxDepth, as encoding/json's limit; no law nests 10000 deep, the agreement test's generated documents do.

mutants.name: flattree-flat-return-is-no-space
mutants.rule: A carriage return is whitespace; the laws' samples have none, the agreement test's odd whitespace and the suite do.

mutants.name: flattree-flat-index-one-past-the-end
mutants.rule: An index equal to the length names nothing; the laws get only places that exist, the agreement test's pointers go one past.
